title: Accessibility Policy
summary: This statement applies to the https://www.literaryworm.com website. LiteraryWorm is committed to ensuring our services are accessible to people with disabilities, so everyone at home can read and listen. We aim to conform with the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2 at Level AA.

sections.heading: Accessibility features
paragraphs: You should be able to change colors, contrast levels, and fonts; zoom in up to 200% without loss of information or functionality; navigate the website with just a keyboard, including keyboard shortcuts in the player; listen to the website using a screen reader, with labelled controls; use the read-along transcript with audiobooks; stop moving images with reduced motion; and turn on underlined links.
The accessibility menu at the top of every page changes text size, theme (dark or light), an easier-to-read font, high contrast, underlined links and reduced motion. Your choices last for the visit.

Every page works with a keyboard alone, and the player has keyboard shortcuts, listed under its controls. Buttons and links are at least 44 pixels square, focus is always visible, and dialogs keep focus inside them and return it when they close.

Screen readers hear labelled controls, headings that outline each page, and announcements when something changes, such as a saved setting or a new club post. Pictures that carry meaning, like shared quote cards, have text alternatives; decorative covers are hidden from screen readers and their titles are always written nearby.

In the reader you can choose the font, size, spacing, margins and theme. Audiobooks have speed control, a sleep timer, skip lengths you choose, and controls on your lock screen and headphones. The player's read-along transcript follows the narration.

sections.heading: Compatibility with assistive technology
paragraphs: Our website is designed to be compatible with screen readers and other assistive technologies, using standard HTML and ARIA, in current versions of Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari. We haven't yet completed testing with each screen reader; if yours has trouble, please tell us.

sections.heading: Conformance status
paragraphs: Status: partially conformant with WCAG 2.2 Level AA. Partially conformant means that most of the website conforms, with the exceptions listed under "What we know isn't perfect yet".
We conducted our most recent accessibility evaluation in October 2026. For more information, see "How we test".

sections.heading: What we know isn't perfect yet
paragraphs: The read-along transcript for some titles is sample text rather than the exact recording, and is hidden while a real recording plays.
Book details and covers from Google Books, and the LibriVox recordings, come from other services; we can't always fix problems in their content.
Books you upload show their text only; images and tables in the original EPUB aren't shown.

sections.heading: How we test
paragraphs: Every change is tested with a keyboard, at phone and desktop sizes, and with automated accessibility checks (Lighthouse accessibility scores of 100) before it's released.

sections.heading: Feedback and contact information
paragraphs: Please let us know if you experience accessibility barriers using our services or need information in an alternative format. Tell us what you were trying to do, which page it was on, and the browser and assistive technology you use.
Email: accessibility@literaryworm.com (mark the subject line "Accessibility").
We aim to reply within five working days, and always within 15 business days, and to fix problems that block reading or listening first. We keep a record of accessibility feedback and our replies.

sections.heading: Enforcement
paragraphs: If you're not satisfied with our response, you can contact the enforcement authority in your country: Germany: BFIT-Bund. France: Défenseur des droits. Ireland: National Disability Authority. Spain: OADIS. Italy: AgID. For other EU countries, contact your national consumer protection authority.

sections.heading: Preparation of this statement
paragraphs: This statement was prepared on 28 October 2026 and is reviewed annually or when we make significant service changes.
For questions about accessibility or this statement, email us at accessibility@literaryworm.com.

title: Privacy Policy
summary: This Privacy Notice for LiteraryWorm ("we," "us," or "our") describes how and why we might access, collect, store, use, and/or share ("process") your personal information when you use our services ("Services"), including when you visit our website at https://www.literaryworm.com or any website of ours that links to this Privacy Notice, or engage with us in other related ways.

sections.heading: Questions or concerns?
paragraphs: Reading this Privacy Notice will help you understand your privacy rights and choices. We are responsible for making decisions about how your personal information is processed. If you do not agree with our policies and practices, please do not use our Services. If you still have any questions or concerns, please contact us at usprivacy@literaryworm.com.

sections.heading: Summary of key points
paragraphs: This summary provides key points from our Privacy Notice; you can find out more details about any of these topics in the numbered sections below.

What personal information do we process? When you visit, use, or navigate our Services, we may process personal information depending on how you interact with us and the Services, the choices you make, and the products and features you use. See section 1.

Do we process any sensitive personal information? Some information may be considered "special" or "sensitive" in certain jurisdictions, for example your racial or ethnic origins, sexual orientation, religious beliefs, biometric or financial data. We don't collect any of those. The only information we hold that some laws treat as sensitive is your account login information.
Do we collect any information from third parties? We do not collect any information from third parties.

How do we process your information? We process your information to provide, improve, and administer our Services, communicate with you, for security and fraud prevention, and to comply with law. We may also process your information for other purposes with your consent. We process your information only when we have a valid legal reason to do so. See section 2.

In what situations and with which parties do we share personal information? Only with the service providers that help us run LiteraryWorm, and in the specific situations described in section 4. We don't sell your personal information or share it for advertising.

How do we keep your information safe? We have adequate organizational and technical processes and procedures in place to protect your personal information. However, no electronic transmission over the internet or information storage technology can be guaranteed to be 100% secure, so we cannot promise or guarantee that hackers, cybercriminals, or other unauthorized third parties will not be able to defeat our security and improperly collect, access, steal, or modify your information. See section 9.
What are your rights? Depending on where you are located geographically, the applicable privacy law may mean you have certain rights regarding your personal information. See section 11.

How do you exercise your rights? The easiest way is in Account, where you can download a copy of your data, change it, or delete it, or by contacting us at usprivacy@literaryworm.com. We will consider and act upon any request in accordance with applicable data protection laws.

sections.heading: 1. What information do we collect?
paragraphs: Personal information you disclose to us. In Short: We collect personal information that you provide to us.
We collect personal information that you voluntarily provide to us when you register on the Services, when you participate in activities on the Services, or otherwise when you contact us.

Personal Information Provided by You. The personal information that we collect depends on the context of your interactions with us and the Services, the choices you make, and the products and features you use. It includes your email address, display name, password, date of birth, contact preferences (marketing emails) and authentication data, and what you read, save and share in the app.
Section 18 lists exactly what we keep.
Sensitive Information. We do not collect biometric data, financial data, or other special categories of personal information.

Payment Data. LiteraryWorm doesn't take payment yet, so we don't collect payment card numbers or billing addresses. If we add paid plans, payment data will be handled and stored by Stripe (https://stripe.com/privacy), and we'll update this notice before we do.
Social Media Login Data. We don't offer registration or log in with social media accounts.
All personal information that you provide to us must be true, complete, and accurate, and you must notify us of any changes to such personal information.

Information automatically collected. In Short: Some information — such as your Internet Protocol (IP) address and browser and device characteristics — is collected automatically when you visit our Services.

Log and Usage Data. Our hosting and backend providers (Vercel and Supabase) automatically record service-related, diagnostic and performance information when you access the Services, in log files. This may include your IP address, browser type, the date and time of requests, the pages and files requested, and error reports. It is used to keep the Services secure and working, not for advertising, and we don't build profiles from it.
Location Data. We don't collect your device's location, and we don't use GPS or similar technologies.

Google API. We use the Google Books API only for book information: our server sends it search words and book ids, never who's asking. Our use of information received from Google APIs will adhere to Google API Services User Data Policy, including the Limited Use requirements.

sections.heading: 2. How do we process your information?
paragraphs: In Short: We process your information to provide, improve, and administer our Services, communicate with you, for security and fraud prevention, and to comply with law. We may also process your information for other purposes only with your prior explicit consent.

To facilitate account creation and authentication and otherwise manage user accounts. We may process your information so you can create and log in to your account, as well as keep your account and household profiles in working order.

To deliver and facilitate delivery of services to the user. We may process your information to provide you with the requested service, such as keeping your place in a book across devices, your bookmarks, highlights, lists, goals and stats.
To respond to user inquiries/offer support to users. We may process your information to respond to your inquiries and solve any potential issues you might have with the requested service.
To send administrative information to you. We may process your information to send you details about your account, changes to our terms and policies, and other similar information.

To enable user-to-user communications. We may process your information if you choose to use any of our offerings that allow for communication with another user, such as reading logs, book clubs and shared lists.
To send you marketing and promotional communications, only if you turned on marketing emails. You can turn them off at any time in Account. For more information, see section 11.
To show you recommendations. Book recommendations and reading stats are worked out in your browser from your own reading; they aren't used for advertising.

To protect our Services. We may process your information as part of our efforts to keep our Services safe and secure, including fraud monitoring and prevention and limiting how often our features can be used.
To save or protect an individual's vital interest. We may process your information when necessary to save or protect an individual's vital interest, such as to prevent harm.
We don't process your information to deliver targeted advertising.

sections.heading: 3. What legal bases do we rely on to process your information?
paragraphs: In Short: We only process your personal information when we believe it is necessary and we have a valid legal reason (i.e., legal basis) to do so under applicable law, like with your consent, to comply with laws, to provide you with services to enter into or fulfill our contractual obligations, to protect your rights, or to fulfill our legitimate business interests.

If you are located in the EU or UK, this section applies to you. The General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and UK GDPR require us to explain the valid legal bases we rely on in order to process your personal information. As such, we may rely on the following legal bases to process your personal information:

Consent. We may process your information if you have given us permission (i.e., consent) to use your personal information for a specific purpose, such as marketing emails or a Kids profile. You can withdraw your consent at any time (see section 11).

Performance of a Contract. We may process your personal information when we believe it is necessary to fulfill our contractual obligations to you, including providing our Services or at your request prior to entering into a contract with you.

Legitimate Interests. We may process your information when we believe it is reasonably necessary to achieve our legitimate business interests and those interests do not outweigh your interests and fundamental rights and freedoms: to diagnose problems and prevent fraudulent activities, and to keep the Services secure and working.

Legal Obligations. We may process your information where we believe it is necessary for compliance with our legal obligations, such as to cooperate with a law enforcement body or regulatory agency, exercise or defend our legal rights, or disclose your information as evidence in litigation in which we are involved.

Vital Interests. We may process your information where we believe it is necessary to protect your vital interests or the vital interests of a third party, such as situations involving potential threats to the safety of any person.

If you are located in Canada, this section applies to you. We may process your information if you have given us specific permission (i.e., express consent) to use your personal information for a specific purpose, or in situations where your permission can be inferred (i.e., implied consent). You can withdraw your consent at any time.

In some exceptional cases, we may be legally permitted under applicable law to process your information without your consent, including, for example: if collection is clearly in the interests of an individual and consent cannot be obtained in a timely way; for investigations and fraud detection and prevention; for business transactions provided certain conditions are met; if it is contained in a witness statement and the collection is necessary to assess, process, or settle an insurance claim; for identifying injured, ill, or deceased persons and communicating with next of kin; if we have reasonable grounds to believe an individual has been, is, or may be victim of financial abuse; if it is reasonable to expect collection and use with consent would compromise the availability or the accuracy of the information and the collection is reasonable for purposes related to investigating a breach of an agreement or a contravention of the laws of Canada or a province; if disclosure is required to comply with a subpoena, warrant, court order, or rules of the court relating to the production of records; if it was produced by an individual in the course of their employment, business, or profession and the collection is consistent with the purposes for which the information was produced; if the collection is solely for journalistic, artistic, or literary purposes; and if the information is publicly available and is specified by the regulations. We may disclose de-identified information for approved research or statistics projects, subject to ethics oversight and confidentiality commitments.

sections.heading: 4. When and with whom do we share your personal information?
paragraphs: In Short: We share information only with the service providers that help us run LiteraryWorm, and in the situations described in this section.
Service providers. Supabase stores the data above and runs our server functions. Vercel hosts the website. Neither may use your data for their own purposes.
Anthropic (Claude) writes book summaries and answers Ask the book questions (see section 6).

Google Books answers searches and book details through our server, which sends only the search words and book ids, never who's asking. LibriVox recordings stream from the Internet Archive, and fonts load from Google Fonts, directly from your browser.

Other members. Reading logs are public, with your display name. Book club posts are seen by the club's members. Lists you share can be read by anyone with the link. Staff with the right access can see account details to run the service and help you.

Business Transfers. We may share or transfer your information in connection with, or during negotiations of, any merger, sale of company assets, financing, or acquisition of all or a portion of our business to another company.

sections.heading: 5. Do we use cookies and other tracking technologies?
paragraphs: In Short: We use only essential cookies and similar technologies, described in our Cookie Policy.
The technologies we use help us maintain the security of our Services and your account, keep you signed in, and let the app work offline.

We don't permit third parties or service providers to use online tracking technologies on our Services for analytics or advertising, and we don't use Google Analytics or any other analytics or advertising service.
Specific information about the technologies we use and how you can refuse certain cookies is set out in our Cookie Policy.

sections.heading: 6. Do we offer artificial intelligence-based products?
paragraphs: In Short: We offer products, features, or tools powered by artificial intelligence, machine learning, or similar technologies.
As part of our Services, we offer features powered by artificial intelligence ("AI Products"). The terms in this Privacy Notice govern your use of the AI Products within our Services.

Use of AI Technologies. We provide the AI Products through one third-party service provider ("AI Service Provider"): Anthropic (Claude). We don't use OpenAI, Hugging Face, Google Cloud AI, DeepSeek or Gemini to process your information. Figma Make was used only to design the app's screens and never receives your information. You must not use the AI Products in any way that violates the terms or policies of the AI Service Provider.

Our AI Products. Book summaries: short and detailed summaries of books in our catalog, written the first time anyone asks, from the book's details; no personal information is sent. Ask the book: answers to your questions about a public-domain book. We send your question and the book's text up to your chapter; we don't send your name, email or account details. Ask the book isn't offered to Kids profiles. Summaries and answers are labelled as written by AI.

How We Process Your Data Using AI. All personal information processed using our AI Products is handled in line with this Privacy Notice and our agreement with the AI Service Provider. We don't use your reading history, notes, uploads or posts to train AI models.

sections.heading: 7. How do we handle your social logins?
paragraphs: We don't offer registration or log in using social media accounts. If we add it, we'll update this Privacy Notice first.

sections.heading: 8. How long do we keep your information?
paragraphs: In Short: We keep your information for as long as necessary to fulfill the purposes outlined in this Privacy Notice unless otherwise required by law.

We will only keep your personal information for as long as it is necessary for the purposes set out in this Privacy Notice, unless a longer retention period is required or permitted by law (such as tax, accounting, or other legal requirements). No purpose in this notice will require us keeping your personal information for longer than the period of time in which users have an account with us.

When we have no ongoing legitimate business need to process your personal information, we will either delete or anonymize such information, or, if this is not possible (for example, because your personal information has been stored in backup archives), then we will securely store your personal information and isolate it from any further processing until deletion is possible.

sections.heading: 9. How do we keep your information safe?
paragraphs: In Short: We aim to protect your personal information through a system of organizational and technical security measures.

We have implemented appropriate and reasonable technical and organizational security measures designed to protect the security of any personal information we process. For example, connections use HTTPS, and access rules in our database let each account read only its own data. However, despite our safeguards and efforts to secure your information, no electronic transmission over the Internet or information storage technology can be guaranteed to be 100% secure, so we cannot promise or guarantee that hackers, cybercriminals, or other unauthorized third parties will not be able to defeat our security and improperly collect, access, steal, or modify your information. Although we will do our best to protect your personal information, transmission of personal information to and from our Services is at your own risk. You should only access the Services within a secure environment.

sections.heading: 10. Do we collect information from minors?
paragraphs: In Short: We do not knowingly collect data from or market to children under 18 years of age or the equivalent age as specified by law in your jurisdiction, except through Kids profiles that a parent or guardian creates on their own account.

Account holders must be 18 or older. We do not knowingly collect, solicit data from, or market to children under 18 years of age or the equivalent age as specified by law in your jurisdiction, nor do we knowingly sell such personal information. By using the Services, you represent that you are at least 18 or the equivalent age as specified by law in your jurisdiction or that you are the parent or guardian of such a minor and consent to such minor dependent's use of the Services through a Kids profile. The Children's Privacy Notice explains what Kids profiles keep.

If we learn that personal information from users less than 18 years of age or the equivalent age as specified by law in your jurisdiction has been collected without that consent, we will deactivate the account and take reasonable measures to promptly delete such data from our records. If you become aware of any such data, please contact us at usprivacy@literaryworm.com.

sections.heading: 11. What are your privacy rights?
paragraphs: In Short: Depending on your state of residence in the US or in some regions, such as the European Economic Area (EEA), United Kingdom (UK), Switzerland, and Canada, you have rights that allow you greater access to and control over your personal information. You may review, change, or terminate your account at any time, depending on your country, province, or state of residence.

In some regions (like the EEA, UK, Switzerland, and Canada), you have certain rights under applicable data protection laws. These may include the right (i) to request access and obtain a copy of your personal information, (ii) to request rectification or erasure; (iii) to restrict the processing of your personal information; (iv) if applicable, to data portability; and (v) not to be subject to automated decision-making. If a decision that produces legal or similarly significant effects is made solely by automated means, we will inform you, explain the main factors, and offer a simple way to request human review. In certain circumstances, you may also have the right to object to the processing of your personal information. You can make such a request by contacting us by using the contact details provided in the section "20. How can you contact us about this notice?" below.
We will consider and act upon any request in accordance with applicable data protection laws.

If you are located in the UK and are unhappy with how we have handled your personal information, you can make a complaint directly to us at usprivacy@literaryworm.com. This is in addition to the rights you have under the UK General Data Protection Regulation and the Data Protection Act 2018.

What happens after you complain: we will acknowledge your complaint within 30 days of receiving it, investigate without unjustifiable or excessive delay, keep you informed of progress and explain the outcome.

If you are not happy with our final response, you can refer your complaint to the Information Commissioner's Office, the UK supervisory authority. Website: ico.org.uk/make-a-complaint. Helpline: 0303 123 1113. Post: Information Commissioner's Office, Wycliffe House, Water Lane, Wilmslow, Cheshire, SK9 5AF.

If you are located in the EEA or UK and you believe we are unlawfully processing your personal information, you also have the right to complain to your Member State data protection authority or UK data protection authority.
If you are located in Switzerland, you may contact the Federal Data Protection and Information Commissioner.

Withdrawing your consent: If we are relying on your consent to process your personal information, which may be express and/or implied consent depending on the applicable law, you have the right to withdraw your consent at any time. You can withdraw your consent at any time in Account (for marketing emails and Kids profiles) or by contacting us by using the contact details provided in the section "20. How can you contact us about this notice?" below.

However, please note that this will not affect the lawfulness of the processing before its withdrawal nor, when applicable law allows, will it affect the processing of your personal information conducted in reliance on lawful processing grounds other than consent.

Opting out of marketing and promotional communications: You can unsubscribe from our marketing and promotional communications at any time by turning off marketing emails in Account, by clicking on the unsubscribe link in the emails that we send, or by contacting us. We may still communicate with you, for example to send you service-related messages that are necessary for the administration and use of your account, to respond to service requests, or for other non-marketing purposes.

Account Information. If you would at any time like to review or change the information in your account or terminate your account, you can log in and go to Account. There you can change your details, download a copy of your data, and delete profiles or your whole account. Deleting your account deletes its information from our databases straight away; copies in our providers' backups are removed when those backups expire.

Cookies and similar technologies: Most Web browsers are set to accept cookies by default. If you prefer, you can usually choose to set your browser to remove cookies and to reject cookies. If you choose to remove cookies or reject cookies, this could affect certain features or services of our Services.
If you have questions or comments about your privacy rights, you may email us at usprivacy@literaryworm.com.

sections.heading: 12. Controls for Do-Not-Track features
paragraphs: Most web browsers and some mobile operating systems and mobile applications include a Do-Not-Track ("DNT") feature or setting you can activate to signal your privacy preference not to have data about your online browsing activities monitored and collected. At this stage, no uniform technology standard for recognizing and implementing DNT signals has been finalized. As such, we do not currently respond to DNT browser signals or any other mechanism that automatically communicates your choice not to be tracked online. We don't track you across other websites in any case. If a standard for online tracking is adopted that we must follow in the future, we will inform you about that practice in a revised version of this Privacy Notice.

California law requires us to let you know how we respond to web browser DNT signals. Because there currently is not an industry or legal standard for recognizing or honoring DNT signals, we do not respond to them at this time.

Global Privacy Control: We recognize and honor Global Privacy Control (GPC) signals. If you use a browser or extension that supports GPC, we will treat this as a valid request to opt out of the sale or sharing of your personal information for targeted advertising purposes under applicable state privacy laws, including the California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA). We don't sell or share personal information, so nothing more needs to change for you. For more information about GPC and how to enable it, visit globalprivacycontrol.org.

sections.heading: 13. Do United States residents have specific privacy rights?
paragraphs: In Short: If you are a resident of California, Colorado, Connecticut, Delaware, Florida, Indiana, Iowa, Kentucky, Maryland, Minnesota, Montana, Nebraska, New Hampshire, New Jersey, Oregon, Rhode Island, Tennessee, Texas, Utah, or Virginia, you may have the right to request access to and receive details about the personal information we maintain about you and how we have processed it, correct inaccuracies, get a copy of, or delete your personal information. You may also have the right to withdraw your consent to our processing of your personal information. These rights may be limited in some circumstances by applicable law. More information is provided below.

Categories of Personal Information We Collect. These are the categories of personal information we have collected in the past twelve (12) months. For a full list of what we process, see sections 1 and 18.

A. Identifiers (such as name, alias, online identifier, Internet Protocol address, email address, and account name): YES. Your email address, display name, account id, and IP address in our providers' logs.

B. Personal information as defined in the California Customer Records statute (name, contact information, education, employment, employment history, and financial information): YES, your display name and email address only.

C. Protected classification characteristics under state or federal law (gender, age, date of birth, race and ethnicity, national origin, marital status, and other demographic data): YES, your date of birth only, to confirm you're 18 or over.
D. Commercial information (transaction information, purchase history, financial details, and payment information): NO. We record which plan you chose, but we take no payment.
E. Biometric information (fingerprints and voiceprints): NO.

F. Internet or other similar network activity (browsing history, search history, online behavior, interest data, and interactions with our and other websites, applications, systems, and advertisements): YES, within LiteraryWorm only: your searches and reading activity on our Services. Not your activity on other websites.
G. Geolocation data (device location): NO.
H. Audio, electronic, sensory, or similar information (images and audio, video or call recordings): NO.
I. Professional or employment-related information: NO.
J. Education Information (student records and directory information): NO.

K. Inferences drawn from collected personal information (a profile or summary of an individual's preferences and characteristics): YES. Book recommendations, worked out in your browser from your own reading and not used for advertising.
L. Sensitive personal information: YES, account login information only. No biometric data.
We will use and retain the personal information in each category for as long as the user has an account with us.

We only collect sensitive personal information, as defined by applicable privacy laws or the purposes allowed by law or with your consent. Sensitive personal information may be used, or disclosed to a service provider or contractor, for additional, specified purposes. You may have the right to limit the use or disclosure of your sensitive personal information. We do not collect or process sensitive personal information for the purpose of inferring characteristics about you.
We may also collect other personal information outside of these categories when you receive help through our customer support channels, or to deliver our Services and respond to your inquiries.
Sources of Personal Information. See section 1. How We Use and Share Personal Information. See sections 2 and 4.

Will your information be shared with anyone else? We may disclose your personal information with our service providers pursuant to a written contract between us and each service provider. See section 4. We may use your personal information for our own business purposes, such as for undertaking internal research for technological development and demonstration. This is not considered to be "selling" of your personal information.

We have not disclosed, sold, or shared any personal information to third parties for a business or commercial purpose in the preceding twelve (12) months. We will not sell or share personal information in the future belonging to website visitors, users, and other consumers.

Your Rights. You have rights under certain US state data protection laws. However, these rights are not absolute, and in certain cases, we may decline your request as permitted by law. These rights include: the right to know whether or not we are processing your personal data; to access your personal data; to correct inaccuracies in your personal data; to request the deletion of your personal data; to obtain a copy of the personal data you previously shared with us; to non-discrimination for exercising your rights; and to opt out of the processing of your personal data if it is used for targeted advertising (or sharing as defined under California's privacy law), the sale of personal data, or profiling in furtherance of decisions that produce legal or similarly significant effects ("profiling").

Depending upon the state where you live, you may also have the right to access the categories of personal data being processed (including in Minnesota); to obtain a list of the categories of third parties to which we have disclosed personal data (including in California, Delaware, and Maryland); to obtain a list of specific third parties to which we have disclosed personal data (including in Minnesota and Oregon); to obtain a list of third parties to which we have sold personal data (including in Connecticut); to review, understand, question, and depending on where you live, correct how personal data has been profiled (including in Connecticut and Minnesota); to limit use and disclosure of sensitive personal data (including in California); and to opt out of the collection of sensitive data and personal data collected through the operation of a voice or facial recognition feature (including in Florida).

How to Exercise Your Rights. To exercise these rights, you can use Account (to download, change or delete your data), email us at usprivacy@literaryworm.com, or use the contact details at the bottom of this document. We will honor your opt-out preferences if you enact the Global Privacy Control (GPC) opt-out signal on your browser.

Under certain US state data protection laws, you can designate an authorized agent to make a request on your behalf. We may deny a request from an authorized agent that does not submit proof that they have been validly authorized to act on your behalf in accordance with applicable laws.

Request Verification. Upon receiving your request, we will need to verify your identity to determine you are the same person about whom we have the information in our system. We will only use personal information provided in your request to verify your identity or authority to make the request. However, if we cannot verify your identity from the information already maintained by us, we may request that you provide additional information for the purposes of verifying your identity and for security or fraud-prevention purposes.

If you submit the request through an authorized agent, we may need to collect additional information to verify your identity before processing your request and the agent will need to provide a written and signed permission from you to submit such request on your behalf.

Appeals. Under certain US state data protection laws, if we decline to take action regarding your request, you may appeal our decision by emailing us at usprivacy@literaryworm.com. We will inform you in writing of any action taken or not taken in response to the appeal, including a written explanation of the reasons for the decisions. If your appeal is denied, you may submit a complaint to your state attorney general.

California "Shine The Light" Law. California Civil Code Section 1798.83, also known as the "Shine The Light" law, permits our users who are California residents to request and obtain from us, once a year and free of charge, information about categories of personal information (if any) we disclosed to third parties for direct marketing purposes and the names and addresses of all third parties with which we shared personal information in the immediately preceding calendar year. We don't disclose personal information to third parties for their direct marketing. If you are a California resident and would like to make such a request, please submit your request in writing to us by using the contact details provided in the section "20. How can you contact us about this notice?" below.

sections.heading: 14. Do other regions have specific privacy rights?
paragraphs: In Short: You may have additional rights based on the country you reside in.
Australia and New Zealand. We collect and process your personal information under the obligations and conditions set by Australia's Privacy Act 1988 and New Zealand's Privacy Act 2020 (Privacy Act).

This Privacy Notice satisfies the notice requirements defined in both Privacy Acts, in particular: what personal information we collect from you, from which sources, for which purposes, and other recipients of your personal information.

If you do not wish to provide the personal information necessary to fulfill their applicable purpose, it may affect our ability to provide our services, in particular to offer you the products or services that you want, respond to or help with your requests, manage your account with us, and confirm your identity and protect your account.
At any time, you have the right to request access to or correction of your personal information. You can make such a request by contacting us by using the contact details provided in section 21.

If you believe we are unlawfully processing your personal information, you have the right to submit a complaint about a breach of the Australian Privacy Principles to the Office of the Australian Information Commissioner and a breach of New Zealand's Privacy Principles to the Office of New Zealand Privacy Commissioner.

Republic of South Africa. At any time, you have the right to request access to or correction of your personal information. You can make such a request by contacting us by using the contact details provided in section 21.

If you are unsatisfied with the manner in which we address any complaint with regard to our processing of personal information, you can contact the office of the regulator, the Information Regulator (South Africa). General enquiries: enquiries@inforegulator.org.za. Complaints (complete POPIA/PAIA form 5): PAIAComplaints@inforegulator.org.za and POPIAComplaints@inforegulator.org.za.

sections.heading: 15. Licensing and selling your information
paragraphs: We don't sell, rent or license your personal information, and we don't share it for advertising. We use it only to run LiteraryWorm for you.
Content you post (reading logs and club posts) stays yours. The Terms of Service explain the limited licence you give us to show it where you posted it.
We don't use your reading history, notes, uploads or posts to train AI models.

sections.heading: 16. How long we keep it
paragraphs: We keep your data while your account is open. Deleting a profile deletes its data, including its uploaded books. Deleting your account deletes everything at once, including your uploads; public logs and club posts go with it.
To protect the service from abuse, we keep short-lived counts of requests, keyed by a one-way hash of your account or network address, and clear them within a day.

sections.heading: 17. Your choices and rights
paragraphs: In Account you can download a copy of your data, change your display name and marketing emails, and delete profiles or your whole account. You can remove any log, post, highlight or upload yourself.
We honour Global Privacy Control. Children's data is covered by the Children's Privacy Notice, and what we keep in your browser by the Cookie Policy.

sections.heading: 18. What we collect
paragraphs: Your account: your email address, display name, password, date of birth (to confirm you're 18 or over), whether you'd like marketing emails, when you accepted the Terms, and your plan. Your password is handled by our sign-in provider and kept only as a one-way hash; we never see it.

Your household: each profile's name, avatar, age rating, favourite genres, daily limit and player settings. A profile PIN is kept only as a one-way hash. For Kids profiles, we keep a record of the parent's consent.

Your reading: your library, reading progress, bookmarks, highlights and notes, ratings, favourites and lists, recent searches, reading goals, time read and listened each day, and the books you finish.

Things you share or add: reading logs (public, with your display name), book club posts (seen by the club's members), lists you choose to share by link, and books you upload (private to the profile that added them; we keep their text only).
Devices: while you're signed in, a short label for each open copy of the app (such as "Chrome on Windows") so you can send a book to another device.

sections.heading: 19. Do we make updates to this notice?
paragraphs: In Short: Yes, we will update this notice as necessary to stay compliant with relevant laws.

We may update this Privacy Notice from time to time. The updated version will be indicated by an updated "Last updated" date at the top of this Privacy Notice. If we make material changes to this Privacy Notice, we may notify you either by prominently posting a notice of such changes or by directly sending you a notification. We encourage you to review this Privacy Notice frequently to be informed of how we are protecting your information.

sections.heading: 20. How can you contact us about this notice?
paragraphs: If you have questions or comments about this notice, you may email us at usprivacy@literaryworm.com.

sections.heading: 21. How can you review, update, or delete the data we collect from you?
paragraphs: Based on the applicable laws of your country or state of residence in the US, you may have the right to request access to the personal information we collect from you, details about how we have processed it, correct inaccuracies, or delete your personal information. You may also have the right to withdraw your consent to our processing of your personal information. These rights may be limited in some circumstances by applicable law.
To review, update, or delete your personal information, go to Account, where you can download a copy of your data, change it, or delete it, or email us at usprivacy@literaryworm.com.

title: Cookie Policy
summary: This Cookie Policy explains how LiteraryWorm ("Company," "we," "us," and "our") uses cookies and similar technologies to recognize you when you visit our website at https://www.literaryworm.com ("Website"). It explains what these technologies are and why we use them, as well as your rights to control our use of them.

sections.heading: About this policy
paragraphs: In some cases we may use cookies to collect personal information, or that becomes personal information if we combine it with other information.

sections.heading: What are cookies?
paragraphs: Cookies are small data files that are placed on your computer or mobile device when you visit a website. Cookies are widely used by website owners in order to make their websites work, or to work more efficiently, as well as to provide reporting information.

Cookies set by the website owner (in this case, LiteraryWorm) are called "first-party cookies." Cookies set by parties other than the website owner are called "third-party cookies." Third-party cookies enable third-party features or functionality to be provided on or through the website (e.g., advertising, interactive content, and analytics). The parties that set these third-party cookies can recognize your computer both when it visits the website in question and also when it visits certain other websites.

sections.heading: Why do we use cookies?
paragraphs: Some cookies are required for technical reasons in order for our Website to operate, and we refer to these as "essential" or "strictly necessary" cookies. LiteraryWorm uses only essential cookies and similar technologies. We don't use cookies to track or target your interests, and we don't let third parties serve cookies through our Website for advertising or analytics. This is described in more detail below.

sections.heading: How can I control cookies?
paragraphs: You have the right to decide whether to accept or reject cookies. Essential cookies cannot be rejected as they are strictly necessary to provide you with services.

Because we use only essential cookies, there is no cookie notification banner or Cookie Preference Center at the moment. If we ever add cookies that aren't essential, we'll ask for your choice first, in a Cookie Preference Center, and update this page.

You may also set or amend your web browser controls to accept or refuse cookies. If you choose to reject cookies, you may still use our Website though your access to some functionality and areas of our Website may be restricted.

The specific types of first- and third-party cookies served through our Website and the purposes they perform are described below (please note that the specific cookies served may vary depending on the specific Online Properties you visit).

sections.heading: Essential website cookies
paragraphs: These cookies are strictly necessary to provide you with services available through our Website and to use some of its features, such as access to secure areas.

__cf_bm. Purpose: Cloudflare places the cookie on end-user devices that access customer sites protected by Bot Management or Bot Fight Mode. Provider: .supabase.co (our backend, Supabase, which is protected by Cloudflare). Service: Cloudflare (see Cloudflare's privacy policy). Type: server cookie. Expires in: 30 minutes.

Some book covers from Google Books, and the audiobook recordings streamed from the Internet Archive, load from those services. When your browser fetches them, those services may set or read their own cookies under their own policies. Blocking third-party cookies in your browser doesn't stop LiteraryWorm working.

sections.heading: Similar technologies: what we keep in your browser
paragraphs: Signed in: when you log in, your browser keeps your sign-in session (in local storage, under literaryworm-session) so you stay signed in after a refresh. It's strictly necessary for your account to work, and it's removed when you log out.
The app itself: so LiteraryWorm opens quickly and without a connection, your browser keeps a copy of the app's own files (its pages, code, icons and app manifest). This holds nothing about you.
Books you save for offline: when you choose Read offline, the book's text, and its audio if you ask, are kept on your device until you remove them from the book's page.
Books you upload: once you've opened one, its text is kept on that device so it keeps working if your connection drops. It's removed when you delete the book or log out.
Everything else, such as reader settings, playback speed, the demo household and uploads made in the demo, stays in the open tab only and is gone when you refresh or close it.

Your library, reading progress, bookmarks, highlights, lists, ratings, reading time, player settings, club activity and uploaded books are saved with your account on our servers (Supabase), not in browser cookies. The Privacy Policy says how we use them, and Account lets you download or delete them.

sections.heading: Do my choices apply on all my devices?
paragraphs: No. Cookie settings you make in your browser, and anything you clear there, apply to that browser on that device only. You'll need to make them again on a different device or browser, and a private or incognito window deletes what it kept when you close it.
Clearing LiteraryWorm's site data signs you out, and books saved for offline will need saving again.

sections.heading: How can I control cookies on my browser?
paragraphs: As the means by which you can refuse cookies through your web browser controls vary from browser to browser, you should visit your browser's help menu for more information. This applies to the most popular browsers: Chrome, Internet Explorer, Firefox, Safari, Edge and Opera.

In addition, most advertising networks offer you a way to opt out of targeted advertising. If you would like to find out more information, please visit the Digital Advertising Alliance, the Digital Advertising Alliance of Canada or the European Interactive Digital Advertising Alliance.

sections.heading: What about other tracking technologies, like web beacons?
paragraphs: Cookies are not the only way to recognize or track visitors to a website. Web beacons (sometimes called "tracking pixels" or "clear gifs") are tiny graphics files that contain a unique identifier that lets a website recognize when someone has visited it or opened an email including them.
LiteraryWorm doesn't use web beacons or tracking pixels on the Website or in its emails.

sections.heading: Do you serve targeted advertising?
paragraphs: No. We don't serve advertising on our Website, and we don't allow third parties to place cookies or web beacons on your computer or mobile device through our Website to serve or measure advertising.

sections.heading: How often will you update this Cookie Policy?
paragraphs: We may update this Cookie Policy from time to time in order to reflect, for example, changes to the cookies we use or for other operational, legal, or regulatory reasons. Please therefore revisit this Cookie Policy regularly to stay informed about our use of cookies and related technologies.
The date at the top of this Cookie Policy indicates when it was last updated.

sections.heading: Where can I get further information?
paragraphs: If you have any questions about our use of cookies or other technologies, please email us at support@literaryworm.com.

title: Children's Privacy Notice
summary: For parents and guardians: what a Kids profile collects, why, who can see it, and how you stay in control. Kids profiles collect only what the service needs, and only after you consent.

sections.heading: Your consent comes first
paragraphs: Only the account holder, who must be 18 or older, can create a Kids profile or move a profile to Kids, and only after reading this notice and confirming with the account password. We keep a record of that consent: when it was given, how, and which version of this notice it was for.

sections.heading: What a Kids profile collects
paragraphs: The profile's first name or nickname and avatar, its age rating and any daily reading limit you set, and its reading: the books in its library, where it is in each book, bookmarks, highlights and notes, ratings, favourites and lists, reading time and goals.
We don't ask a child for their email, full name, address, photo, location or any other contact details.

sections.heading: What a Kids profile can't do
paragraphs: Kids profiles see only books rated for children. They can't write public reading logs, join or start book clubs, share lists by link, upload books, ask the book's AI assistant, make purchases or change account settings. A grown-up's password is needed to open Account or to allow extra time past a daily limit.

sections.heading: Who sees it
paragraphs: A Kids profile's reading is private to your account. It isn't shown to other members, isn't used for advertising, and is never sold, rented or licensed. Our hosting providers (Supabase and Vercel) store it only to run LiteraryWorm for you.

sections.heading: Your choices as a parent
paragraphs: From Account you can see and download the profile's data, change its limits, add a PIN to other profiles so a child can't open them, move the profile to another age rating, or delete it, which deletes everything it collected. You can withdraw consent at any time by deleting the profile.

title: Your Privacy Choices
summary: LiteraryWorm doesn't sell or share personal information for advertising and uses no non-essential cookies (see the Cookie Policy), so there's nothing to opt out of there. Global Privacy Control is honoured. Here are the choices you do have.

sections.heading: Selling and sharing
paragraphs: We don't sell, rent or license your personal information, and we don't share it for cross-context behavioural advertising. If your browser sends a Global Privacy Control signal, we treat it as a request to opt out, and nothing changes because we already don't do either.

sections.heading: Cookies and browser storage
paragraphs: We set no cookies of our own and no advertising or analytics cookies. The Cookie Policy lists the strictly necessary things your browser keeps, such as your sign-in session, and how to clear them.

sections.heading: Emails and notifications
paragraphs: Turn emails about new releases and offers on or off in Account → Preferences. Service emails, like password resets, always arrive. Book club alerts can be turned off for each club on its page, and browser notifications only appear if you allow them.

sections.heading: Your data
paragraphs: In Account you can download a copy of your data, correct your display name, and delete profiles or your whole account. Reading logs, club posts, highlights and uploads can each be deleted whenever you like. The Privacy Policy explains what we keep and for how long.

title: Terms of Service
summary: The agreement between you and LiteraryWorm: who can have an account, how membership works, what you may do with the books, who owns what, and the licence you give us for what you post.

sections.heading: Your account
paragraphs: Account holders must be 18 or older. You may add profiles for people in your household, including Kids profiles with your consent, and you're responsible for how they're used.
Keep your password private. You can change it, and delete your account, from Account at any time.

sections.heading: Membership
paragraphs: Plans renew automatically each month until you cancel, which you can do online at any time; reading continues until the end of the period you've paid for. You can pause and resume from Account.
LiteraryWorm is currently a demonstration: choosing a plan saves it to your account, but no payment is taken.

sections.heading: Your licence to read and listen
paragraphs: While your membership is active, we give you a personal, non-exclusive, non-transferable, revocable licence to read and listen to the books in LiteraryWorm for your own and your household's non-commercial use, in the app.

You may not copy, sell, share, broadcast or publicly perform the books, remove or get around any protection on them, or use them to train AI models. Books saved for offline reading stay in the app on your device.
This licence doesn't apply to public-domain works themselves, which anyone may use freely; it covers our app, our edition and our service.

sections.heading: Who owns the books and the app
paragraphs: Public-domain titles: the texts come from Project Gutenberg and the recordings from LibriVox, whose volunteers release their recordings into the public domain. These works are in the public domain in the United States; they may not be everywhere, so check your country's rules before using them outside LiteraryWorm.
Other LiteraryWorm titles show sample pages, not the published books. Book details and covers from Google Books belong to their publishers and rights holders and are shown under Google's terms.
Summaries and Ask the book answers are written by AI (Claude) and labelled so. They may be wrong; they're provided for your own reading and may not be republished as LiteraryWorm's.
The LiteraryWorm name, logo, design and software belong to LiteraryWorm. Using the service doesn't give you any rights in them beyond these Terms.

sections.heading: What you post, and the licence you give us
paragraphs: You own what you write: reading logs, club posts, list names and descriptions, notes and highlights.

So we can run the features you use, you give LiteraryWorm a worldwide, non-exclusive, royalty-free licence to store, copy and display what you post, only where and to whom you posted it (logs on the book's public page with your display name, club posts to the club, shared lists to anyone with the link). The licence ends when you delete the content or your account, except for copies already made by others, such as someone else's screenshot.
Notes, highlights and private lists are never shown to anyone else.

sections.heading: Books you upload
paragraphs: Upload only books you have the right to read in this way, such as DRM-free books you've bought or works in the public domain. Don't upload books you don't have rights to, and don't remove DRM to upload them.
Your uploads stay private to the profile that added them. We store their text only to show it to you, claim no rights in them, and delete them when you do or when you delete the profile or account.

sections.heading: Rules, changes and ending
paragraphs: Don't post anything unlawful, hateful, harassing or infringing, impersonate others, spam clubs, or try to break or overload the service. We may remove content that breaks these rules and suspend accounts that keep doing so, including repeat copyright infringers (see Copyright/DMCA).
LiteraryWorm is provided as is. We'll tell you before changing these Terms in ways that matter, and you can cancel or delete your account at any time.

title: Copyright/DMCA
summary: How LiteraryWorm respects copyright, which works are in the public domain, and how a rights holder can report content they believe infringes, under the Digital Millennium Copyright Act (DMCA).

sections.heading: Our books and their licences
paragraphs: Public-domain titles use texts from Project Gutenberg and recordings from LibriVox, which LibriVox volunteers release into the public domain. These works are in the public domain in the United States, where LiteraryWorm operates. Our copies leave out Project Gutenberg's own header, footer and licence text.
Other titles show sample pages written for LiteraryWorm, not the published books, and book details and covers come from Google Books under Google's terms.
If you believe any of this is wrong, for example that a work isn't in the public domain, tell us using the steps below and we'll look into it promptly.

sections.heading: What people post or upload
paragraphs: Reading logs, club posts and shared lists are written by members, who keep their rights in them. Books members upload are private to their own profile and aren't shown to anyone else; members must have the right to read them that way (see the Terms of Service).

sections.heading: Reporting infringement
paragraphs: If you believe something on LiteraryWorm infringes your copyright, send our designated agent a written notice that includes: your physical or electronic signature; the work you believe is infringed; the material on LiteraryWorm you want removed and where it is (a link helps); your name, address, phone number and email; a statement that you believe in good faith the use isn't authorised by the copyright owner, its agent or the law; and a statement, under penalty of perjury, that the notice is accurate and that you are, or are authorised to act for, the owner.
Our designated agent's name, postal address, phone number and email, as registered with the U.S. Copyright Office, will be listed here before launch.
We remove or disable access to the material, tell the member who posted it, and keep a record of the notice.

sections.heading: Counter-notices
paragraphs: If your content was removed and you believe that was a mistake or that you had the right to post it, you may send a counter-notice with: your signature; what was removed and where it was; a statement, under penalty of perjury, that you believe in good faith it was removed by mistake or misidentification; your name, address and phone number; and your consent to the jurisdiction of the federal court for your address (or, outside the United States, any district where LiteraryWorm may be found) and to accept service from the person who sent the notice.
We forward it to the person who sent the notice and may restore the content in 10 to 14 business days unless they tell us they've filed a court action.

sections.heading: Repeat infringers and false claims
paragraphs: We close the accounts of members who repeatedly infringe copyright.
Knowingly misrepresenting that material infringes, or that it was removed by mistake, can make you liable for damages under the DMCA, so please be sure before you send a notice or counter-notice.

title: Help
summary: Answers to common questions about reading, listening, your library and your account, and how to report a problem.

sections.heading: Where do the books come from?
paragraphs: LiteraryWorm uses the Google Books API to show book details and covers when you browse and search, so you can find almost any book, save it to your library and write about it.
The books you can read and listen to in full are public-domain classics: texts from Project Gutenberg and recordings from LibriVox. Other LiteraryWorm titles show sample pages.

sections.heading: Can I read my own books?
paragraphs: Yes. In My Library → Uploads, add an EPUB you own that has no DRM. For example, buy a book that the publisher sells DRM-free on Google Play Books, download its EPUB from your Google Play Books library, then upload it to LiteraryWorm. Many publishers and stores sell DRM-free books, and public-domain EPUBs are free from Project Gutenberg and Standard Ebooks.

Your upload opens in the reader with your place, bookmarks and highlights, and once you've opened it on a device, it keeps working there if your connection drops. Books with DRM can't be uploaded, and removing DRM to upload a book isn't allowed (see the Terms of Service).

sections.heading: Reading and listening
paragraphs: Open a book from its page with Read or Listen. Your place is shared between the two and across your devices. The mini-player keeps a book playing while you browse, and its controls also work from your lock screen and headphones.
To read or listen without a connection, choose Read offline on a public-domain book's page.

sections.heading: Your account and household
paragraphs: Each person at home can have their own profile, with its own library and recommendations. Lock a profile with a PIN, set daily limits for younger readers, and change your plan, password or emails in Account. You can cancel or pause online at any time.

sections.heading: Report a problem
paragraphs: Tell us what you were doing, the page you were on, and your device and browser. Contact details for support will be published here before launch; until then, LiteraryWorm is a demonstration.

sections.heading: Services
paragraphs: Website and app: working normally.
Accounts, libraries and reading progress: working normally.
Book search and details (Google Books): working normally.
Audiobook recordings (Internet Archive): working normally.
Summaries and Ask the book (AI): working normally.

sections.heading: If something isn't working
paragraphs: Your reading progress is saved on your device first and sent when the connection returns, so you won't lose your place. Books saved for offline keep working without a connection.
